tools.name: MapLibre GL JS
tools.rationale: Current WebGL map engine already passes real-browser smoke tests and supports the required GeoJSON/vector/raster model without a frontend rewrite.

tools.name: PostgreSQL/PostGIS
tools.rationale: Canonical production store for spatial queries, persistence and analytical joins; replacing it would add a second spatial data plane.

tools.name: HashiCorp Terraform
tools.license: BUSL-1.1 for current Terraform distributions; provider licenses reviewed separately
tools.rationale: One declarative provisioning authority prevents drift from imperative gcloud/Replit scripts. The Google provider is pinned and write-only secret attributes keep supported secret payloads out of state.

tools.name: GitHub OIDC + Google Workload Identity Federation
tools.rationale: Deploys an already-green immutable commit without storing long-lived Google service-account JSON keys in GitHub or development environments.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.rationale: Exercises the authenticated page in a real Chromium runtime and catches map/browser integration failures that unit tests cannot.

tools.name: Trivy
tools.rationale: Gates the production image and repository secret/misconfiguration posture, avoiding a duplicate scanner stack.

tools.name: pip-audit
tools.rationale: Python-specific dependency advisory gate complements rather than duplicates the container scan.

tools.name: AISStream
tools.rationale: Current decoded real-time feed is integrated server-side with bounded strategic coverage and no browser credential exposure.

tools.name: pyais
tools.rationale: Mature AIVDM/AIVDO decoder with TCP/UDP/file support; installing it before a raw NMEA source exists would create an unused dependency.

tools.name: AIS-catcher
tools.rationale: Strong SDR receiver option for future owned coastal sensors; keep isolated from proprietary server code and review GPL obligations before deployment.

tools.name: protomaps/PMTiles
tools.license: BSD-3-Clause reference implementations; PMTiles specification public domain/CC0 where applicable
tools.rationale: Official PMTiles is designed for single-file range-request tile archives on commodity object storage and supports MapLibre directly. It fits GCS and can remove runtime dependence on public raster tile servers without adding a tile backend. Basemap source-data licensing and attribution remain a separate mandatory review.

tools.name: OpenSanctions Yente
tools.rationale: Could improve alias/entity matching, but official issuing-authority sanctions data remains canonical and an aggregator must not create a second legal truth source.

tools.name: koala73/worldmonitor
tools.rationale: Useful reference for multi-stream intelligence, map performance and source freshness; AGPL code is not copied into this proprietary repository.

tools.name: cognis-digital/conflictwatch
tools.rationale: Broad source catalog is valuable for discovery, but every upstream source must pass independent endpoint, rights, cadence and evidence-role review.

tools.name: Trafilatura
tools.rationale: Focused main-text extraction remains the lowest-cost first step for ordinary articles before browser escalation.

tools.name: Crawl4AI
tools.rationale: Current actively maintained crawler supports async crawling, browser-backed extraction and structured Markdown; use only after source rights, robots/terms and network policies are satisfied.

tools.name: Scrapling
tools.rationale: Useful adaptive selector/parser fallback when normal extraction breaks. Stealth, anti-bot bypass and access-control circumvention features are disabled by project policy.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.rationale: Already the browser E2E primary; reuse the same controlled browser stack for JS-rendered source acquisition rather than adding another browser runtime.

tools.name: webrecorder/browsertrix-crawler
tools.rationale: Use for high-fidelity dynamic-page preservation into WARC when provenance value justifies the heavier browser capture. Not a general crawler replacement.

tools.name: Docling
tools.rationale: Adds structured parsing for PDFs and office documents, including layout and tables, without forcing OCR-first processing.

tools.name: getzep/graphiti
tools.rationale: Strong fit for temporal facts, validity windows and provenance, but only as a reconstructible derived graph. PostgreSQL/RAW evidence and approved Second Brain knowledge remain authoritative.

tools.name: reconurge/flowsint
tools.rationale: Use its graph investigation and enricher interaction patterns as UX reference for the native Investigation Workspace; do not deploy a parallel OSINT application.

tools.name: flowintel/flowintel
tools.rationale: Useful reference for cases, tasks, audit trail and analyst workflow, but overlaps the planned Investigation Workspace and AGPL code should not enter the proprietary runtime.

tools.name: Arize Phoenix
tools.license: Elastic-2.0 / upstream project terms review required
tools.rationale: Provides OpenTelemetry/OpenInference tracing, datasets and experiments for agent decisions without becoming an evidence source.

tools.name: Promptfoo
tools.rationale: Complements Phoenix with deterministic regression suites and adversarial prompt-injection/tool-misuse testing; does not replace runtime policy enforcement.

tools.name: Open Policy Agent
tools.rationale: Moves authorization and source/tool/network decisions out of LLM judgment into auditable deterministic policy.

tools.name: Stacklok ToolHive
tools.rationale: Provides isolation and policy boundaries for external MCP servers. Internal deterministic functions should remain direct code paths rather than being converted to MCP.

tools.name: OASIS cti-python-stix2
tools.rationale: Use the OASIS library to serialize/deserialize STIX 2.1 at boundaries; the internal Entity/Event/Claim/Evidence/Relationship schema remains canonical.

tools.name: OpenCTI
tools.rationale: Retain STIX-like entities, relationships, first/last seen and confidence concepts without deploying a second CTI platform.

tools.name: MapLibre Martin
tools.rationale: Can serve vector tiles directly from PostGIS/PMTiles efficiently, but adds another service and is unnecessary until measured map/API scale requires it.

tools.name: Snyk Agent Scan / MCPRadar class
tools.rationale: Useful for periodic external validation of MCP/tool poisoning coverage, but overlaps the chosen isolation, policy and red-team stack and some scanners may execute discovered MCP servers.
